claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported terminal strain of approximately 13.5%.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has limited tensile ductility.
Adding approximately 4 at% Cr to HfZrTiTa0.53 will promote formation of a Laves phase in addition to the BCC phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase in HfZrTiTa0.53 will have a discontinuous, reticulated morphology within the BCC matrix.
Cr addition and the resulting Laves phase will provide solid-solution and precipitation strengthening.
The reticulated Laves phase will redistribute local strain in Cr-modified HfZrTiTa0.53.
The reticulated Laves phase will impede crack initiation and propagation in Cr-modified HfZrTiTa0.53.
Approximately 4 at% Cr will improve the tensile ductility and uniform elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The tensile ductility or uniform elongation will increase by at least approximately 20% relative to the stated 13.5% baseline.
The Cr-modified alloy will retain yield strength within 5% of the HfZrTiTa0.53 baseline.
The Cr-modified alloy will retain impact-triggered chemical energy release within 5% of the HfZrTiTa0.53 baseline.
The original HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has documented energetic performance in impact tests.
The proposed effect is expected at room temperature under tensile loading at a strain rate around 10^-3 s^-1.
In HfMoTaTiZr, 4.2 at% Cr produced a Laves phase in addition to the BCC phase and formed a reticulated Laves structure.
In HfMoTaTiZr, Cr addition concurrently increased strength and fracture strain, with fracture strain improving by 20.6%.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is initially identified only as terminal strain associated with the reported compression response, but the predicted outcome and baseline subsequently treat it as baseline tensile ductility. Terminal or compressive fracture strain is not interchangeable with tensile ductility or uniform elongation.
